chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Al-Hussein ibn Zyad, from Davood ibn Kaseer al-Ruqqi, who said:

While we were sitting in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), a man passed by us with a swallow in his hand having its head chopped off. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) stood up to him until he took it from his hand, then threw it on the ground, and said: 'Did your learned men or your jurisprudents command you to do this?'

My father has informed me, from my grandfather (peace be upon them both), that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the killing of six: the bee, the ant, the frog, the shrike, the hoopoe, and the swallow.
As for the bee, it eats pure things and produces pure things, and it is the one to whom God the Exalted revealed (inspiration). It is neither of the jinn nor of the humans.

As for the ant, there was a famine during the time of Solomon and David (peace be upon them), so they went out seeking rain. Behold, they saw an ant standing on its two feet, with its hand raised to the sky, saying: 'O God, we are a creation from Your creation, we have no need for Your bounty, so provide for us from Yourself, and do not hold us accountable for the sins of the foolish children of Adam.'
So Solomon said to them: 'Return to your places, for God the Blessed and Exalted has rained for you due to the supplication of others.'

As for the frog, when fire was kindled against Abraham (peace be upon him), the creatures of the earth complained to God the Exalted and asked His permission to pour water upon it. God did not grant permission to any of them except the frog, so two-thirds of it burnt and one-third remained.
As for the hoopoe, it was the guide of Solomon (peace be upon him) to the Queen of Bilqis.
As for the shrike, it was the guide of Adam (peace be upon him) from the land of Serandib to the land of Jeddah for a month.

As for the swallow, its circling in the sky is out of sorrow for what was done to the Household of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and its recitation is the reading of 'Al-Hamd Lillahi Rabb al-Alameen'. Do you not see it saying: 'Wa al-dalleen' (And those who go astray)?
ai.seo_question: What are the six animals forbidden to be killed in Shia tradition and why?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the prohibition against killing six specific animals by linking their natural behaviors to divine wisdom and cosmic events. The text highlights the bee's divine inspiration, the ant's supplication during Solomon's era, the frog's intercession for Abraham, and uniquely attributes the swallow's flight to mourning for the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the connection between creation and the Prophet's household.
